title: Knowledge check: API Documentation with OpenAPI

questions.prompt: In API Documentation with OpenAPI, which statement best describes Documenting paths and methods?
options: Connect this syllabus point to API Documentation with OpenAPI: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
questions.answer_key: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
questions.explanation: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying API Documentation with OpenAPI?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
questions.explanation: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.

questions.prompt: A change related to API Documentation with OpenAPI appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
